headline: First uranium consignment arrives for Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant
summary: The nuclear fuel arrived from Russia via a special chartered cargo flight and is being transported to the project site under heavy Army security.
details: The first batch of uranium for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has arrived in Dhaka from Russia via a special chartered cargo flight that landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport last night.
A special security unit of the Bangladesh Army is managing the transport of the nuclear fuel in three special lorries to the project site.
To ensure safe passage, the 200-kilometre highway from Dhaka airport to Rooppur has been designated as a 'green passage', with police restricting vehicle movement in one lane.
The convoy, which crossed the Jamuna Bridge at approximately 9:10 am today, is being moved under tight security arrangements.
According to plant officials, the fuel will be stored at the project site upon arrival.
Chief of administration Md Golam Mahabub stated that a total of nine flights will be delivered to meet the requirements of Unit-1 and the commissioning of Unit-2.
caption:
Russia has delivered the first shipment of uranium to Bangladesh. The fuel is now moving toward Rooppur under heavy Army security.

The first batch of uranium for the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has arrived in Dhaka from Russia via a special chartered cargo flight that landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport last night.

A special security unit of the Bangladesh Army is managing the transport of the nuclear fuel in three special lorries to the project site.

To ensure safe passage, the 200-kilometre highway from Dhaka airport to Rooppur has been designated as a 'green passage', with police restricting vehicle movement in one lane.

The convoy, which crossed the Jamuna Bridge at approximately 9:10 am today, is being moved under tight security arrangements.

According to plant officials, the fuel will be stored at the project site upon arrival.

Chief of administration Md Golam Mahabub stated that a total of nine flights will be delivered to meet the requirements of Unit-1 and the commissioning of Unit-2.

headline_marked: 63-run loss: [[Bangladesh miss out on Bronze]] at Asian Games
headline: 63-run loss: Bangladesh miss out on Bronze at Asian Games
summary: The Tigers suffer a heavy defeat to a second-string Sri Lankan side, returning home empty-handed for the first time in the tournament's history.
details: Bangladesh suffered a 63-run defeat to a second-string Sri Lanka side in the Bronze-deciding third-place playoff at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin.
The Litton Das-led side were bowled out for 102 in 17.3 overs, failing to reach the target of 166. Sri Lanka posted 165 for nine in 20 overs.
The Tigers experienced a catastrophic early collapse, losing four wickets for just 18 runs in the first 3.5 overs, with openers Saif Hassan and Tanzid Tamim and skipper Litton Das failing to score.
Nasum Ahmed top-scored for Bangladesh with 26 off 28 balls, while Parvez Hossain Emon (20) and Yasir Ali (21) provided minor resistance.
For Sri Lanka, Tharindu Ratnayake starred with 65 off 32 deliveries, and four bowlers—Nuwan Thushara, Tharindu Ratnayake, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, and Wanuja Sahan—took two wickets each.
This marks the first time Bangladesh cricketers will return home empty-handed from the Asian Games, having previously won gold in 2010.
caption:
Empty-handed for the first time. Bangladesh loses the Bronze medal match to Sri Lanka by 63 runs.

Bangladesh suffered a 63-run defeat to a second-string Sri Lanka side in the Bronze-deciding third-place playoff at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin.

The Litton Das-led side were bowled out for 102 in 17.3 overs, failing to reach the target of 166. Sri Lanka posted 165 for nine in 20 overs.

The Tigers experienced a catastrophic early collapse, losing four wickets for just 18 runs in the first 3.5 overs, with openers Saif Hassan and Tanzid Tamim and skipper Litton Das failing to score.

Nasum Ahmed top-scored for Bangladesh with 26 off 28 balls, while Parvez Hossain Emon (20) and Yasir Ali (21) provided minor resistance.

For Sri Lanka, Tharindu Ratnayake starred with 65 off 32 deliveries, and four bowlers—Nuwan Thushara, Tharindu Ratnayake, Vijayakanth Viyaskanth, and Wanuja Sahan—took two wickets each.

This marks the first time Bangladesh cricketers will return home empty-handed from the Asian Games, having previously won gold in 2010.
